escalations.finding: The five spatial upscaler ONNX graphs are published by their upstream repository under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0. CC BY-NC-SA is not an OSI-approved licence.
escalations.consequence: The grant and the condition must not be conflated. Section 2(a)(1) licenses reproduction and sharing 'for NonCommercial purposes only'. Section 1(k) defines NonCommercial as 'not primarily intended for or directed towards commercial advantage or monetary compensation'. The recorded intended use of this project is private, local and non-commercial, so USING these weights on the owner's own machine is within the located grant, and it engages no ShareAlike condition because nothing is shared. REDISTRIBUTION is a separate act: placing the graphs in a shipped bundle is a Share, which triggers section 3(a) attribution, section 3(b) share-alike and the section 2(b)(3) royalty reservation, and it falls outside the recorded scope regardless of its non-commercial character. Separately, the TensorRT SLA and CUDA SLA each contain a clause (1.2.5) forbidding use of the SDK in a manner that would cause it to become subject to an open source software licence; whether a given arrangement of model weights and NVIDIA redistributables in one bundle engages that clause is likewise a question for the rights owner. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is not by itself a licence on the NVIDIA SDK - the two instruments govern different components - so no incompatibility is asserted.
escalations.missingEvidence: if redistribution is ever contemplated, a recorded decision by this project's rights owner on (a) whether the product remains NonCommercial at the moment of distribution, and (b) how the Attribution, ShareAlike and warranty-disclaimer obligations are discharged in the shipped notices. Neither question arises for the private local use that is actually in scope today.
escalations.citationCorrection: An earlier revision of this file cited the NonCommercial definition as section 1(j). In the located text of CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, section 1(j) defines 'Licensor'; NonCommercial is defined in section 1(k). Corrected here and in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

installedBundleInventory.purpose: M03's per-file record. Every binary in the installed private native bundle is listed here with the source it was actually attributed to, the licence as actually located, and one of the three redistribution decisions. This is a RECORD of decisions, not a grant: no row here creates permission, and ESC-1/ESC-2/ESC-3 remain open exactly as before.
whatThisIsNot: It is not a licence clearance. A row marked cleared means the located licence text permits redistribution and its conditions are recorded; it is not legal advice and does not mean the conditions are already satisfied.

It is not a release pin. The sha256 values are the measurements already published in the installed bundle manifest, reproduced here so the mapping is checkable against the files on disk. They are descriptive identity of the shipped bytes, not a reproduction claim from any source revision.

It is not a rights grant for this project's integration code or for anything else. The owner's 2026-10-04 grant covers this project's own code only (projectIntegrationGrant) and clears no third-party component.
installedBundleInventory.scope: The private, locally installed bundle native-0.1.0-dev.2 at %LOCALAPPDATA%/Mikai/Mikai Wrapper/native/runtime/native-0.1.0-dev.2, which is what current-native points at. 83 files, 80 DLLs and 3 EXEs. Read-only inspection: no file was modified, moved, re-hashed into a pin, or executed.
installedBundleInventory.verificationMethod: Each of the 83 recorded sha256 values was recomputed from the file on disk and matched. Attribution was then established per file: 36 mpv-deps DLLs by exact digest match against the pinned MSYS2 package archive index; 17 self-built cohort binaries (the 14 ggml-cpu variants plus ggml-0, ggml-base-0 and libwhisper-1) by exact digest match against the outputs of this repository's own ggml/whisper build; the 13 rebuilt GNU-runtime-free DLLs by digest match against this repository's own relink outputs plus an export-set comparison against the prefix originals. The remaining files were attributed by acquisition route: the core and the ABI-8 shims and the two preparation helpers by exact digest match against this repository's own builds, the CUDA runtime against NVIDIA's published redistributable, TensorRT and ONNX Runtime and DirectML against their pinned vendor packages, and the Microsoft CRT against the pinned vc_redist installer payload.
installedBundleInventory.digestSummary: Every one of the 83 digests was independently recomputed from the installed file and matched the manifest. 36 + 17 + 13 + 5 (this repository's own core, aji.dll, aji_trt.dll, mikai_native_prep.exe, mikai_native_verify.exe) + 1 (cudart) + 3 (TensorRT) + 3 (ORT/DirectML) + 4 (CRT) = 83. native_inspect.exe is the one binary with no independently recomputed input: it is a project-owned tool built by the root CMake in the Qt/MinGW cohort and its only prior copy in the SDK tree predates this build, so its provenance rests on codePaths plus the build record, not on a digest match.

installedBundleInventory.closureFinding: Every static import of every one of the 83 files resolves either inside the bundle, to an api-ms/ext-ms API set, or to a Windows system DLL. No file in the bundle imports a third-party DLL that the bundle does not ship, and none of the 80 DLLs imports libstdc++-6, libgcc_s_seh-1 or libwinpthread-1 - so the native closure cannot collide with the Qt GNU cohort. What the bundle DOES import from outside itself is named per row under importsNeedingAnExternalProvider, and every such name is a Windows system library or a driver-supplied library (nvcuda via the CUDA driver, Qt6Core for the project-owned inspect tool). That is a system dependency, not a missing third-party binary.
installedBundleInventory.selfContainmentLimit: ggml_backend_load_all resolves CPU backend DLLs by searching the executable's own directory and the current working directory, not via AddDllDirectory. The 14 ggml-cpu-*.dll files sitting beside the core is therefore necessary but NOT by itself proof that the variant set resolves on an arbitrary machine; that remains a run-time question and is not claimed here.

unknownsAndGaps: The Microsoft CRT EULA text was not recovered from the pinned installer payload, so the licence terms are identified by acquisition route only. Recorded as missing evidence, not as a grant.

inBundleSemantics.meaning: inBundle answers 'may this component go into a DISTRIBUTABLE bundle?', not 'is this file present in the locally installed private bundle?'. The two differ for the blocked components and confusing them would either hide ESC-1 or pretend it away.
inBundleSemantics.privateInstalledInstance: The installed private bundle native-0.1.0-dev.2 does contain aji.dll and aji_trt.dll, built locally from the unlicensed upstream source. They are present for the owner's own private use and are marked inBundle false because no redistribution clearance exists for them.
inBundleSemantics.howToCheckPresence: installedBundleInventory.files[].componentId maps every one of the 83 installed files to its component, so presence and shipping decision are both explicit per file and neither has to be inferred from the other.
